free_tier.stated: The cheapest plan the vendor's pages let you order is Gigabit VPS 1 at USD 21 a year: 1 fair-share core, 1 GB RAM, 10 GB SSD, 1 IPv4 plus IPv6, 1 TB of bandwidth, in Los Angeles, Salt Lake City, Portland, New York, Miami and Dallas. The Premium Ryzen page prices RYZEN 512 MB at USD 24 a year with 1 fair-share core at 3.5 GHz+, 512 MB RAM, 10 GB NVMe, 1 IPv4 plus a /64 IPv6 and 500 GB at 1 Gbit, which is the same shape the tracker lists at USD 17.99 a year. The Special Ryzen Promo store page shows every tier 'Out of Stock', including Ryzen SP1 at USD 3.00 a month.

egress.terms: 1 TB a month on Gigabit VPS 1 and 500 GB a month on RYZEN 512 MB, at 1 Gbit; no overage rate is published on either page read
egress.free_allowance: 1 TB a month on the USD 21 a year plan

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: KVM with root, rDNS and a VPS control panel, on a Singapore-registered company with US and EU locations; SSH and the client area, no API documented on the pages read
chaining: USD 21 a year works out under USD 2 a month for a machine that can hold a scheduler, a monitor or a small crawler front end in six US cities; the 10 GB disk and 1 TB cap keep it away from anything that stores or serves bulk bytes

limits.value: 1 TB a month on Gigabit VPS 1 and 500 GB on RYZEN 512 MB, both against 10 GB of disk; the byte allowance is small enough that a daytime crawler meets it quickly, and no overage rate is published
